'''Harry Lehmann''' (21 March 1924 in [[Güstrow]]{{spaced ndash}}22 November 1998 in [[Hamburg]]) was a German [[physicist]].<ref>{{cite news|author=Mack, Gerhard|url=http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/28010|title=Harry Lehmann 1924-98|newspaper=CERN Courier|date=30 April 1999}}</ref> Known for his work on [[Correlation function (quantum field theory)|correlation functions]] in [[quantum field theory]].

==Biography==
Lehmann studied physics at [[Rostock]] and the [[Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin]].

In 1952 he worked at the [[Max-Planck-Institut]] in [[Göttingen]], and spent a year in [[Copenhagen]] and from 1956 worked in [[Hamburg]].

In 1967 he won the [[Max Planck Medal]]  for extraordinary achievements in [[theoretical physics]]. It is awarded annually by the [[Deutsche Physikalische Gesellschaft]] ({{langx|de|German Physical Society}}).

He had a strong collaboration with [[Wolfhart Zimmermann]] and [[Kurt Symanzik]] that led to the development of the [[LSZ reduction formula|Lehmann–Symanzik–Zimmermann reduction formula]] or LSZ formula after their initials. They were referred as the Field Club ({{Langx|de|Feldverein}}) by [[Wolfgang Pauli]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mack |first=Gerhard |date=1984-05-01 |title=Kurt Symanzik |url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/article/37/5/102/403511/Kurt-Symanzik |journal=Physics Today |language=en |volume=37 |issue=5 |pages=102–103 |doi=10.1063/1.2916220 |issn=0031-9228|doi-access=free |bibcode=1984PhT....37e.102M |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
